1.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this as a an indirect quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh says that the house of Jacob should hear this, they who are]
The command **Hear** is plural here because Yahweh is addressing all the people of Israel. If your language distinguishes singular and plural command forms, use a plural form here.

The expression **called** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the ones whom people call by the name of Israel]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the ancestry of the people as if it were **the waters of Judah** from which they flowed. He means that they are descended from Judah. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from the line of Judah]

Here, **the name of Yahweh** represents Yahweh’s authority. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [by the authority of Yahweh]
The pronoun **they** refers to the people of Israel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [these people make one remember]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **truth** and **righteousness**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [but not truthfully and not righteously]

The terms **truth** and **righteousness** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [but not according to what is true and right]

2.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [Because]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **holiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [after the holy city]
Yahweh is using this possessive form to mean the God whom the people of Israel worship. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the God whom Israel worships]
Here, **his name** represents who Yahweh is. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [whose name is Yahweh of Armies]
Yahweh is using this possessive form to mean that he commands vast armies. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh, who commands the armies]

3.note: Yahweh is using the adjective **former** as a noun to mean a certain kind of thing. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [The former things]

The implication is that this refers to events that Yahweh predicted long ago, which then came true. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [The things I predicted long ago]
The pronoun **they** refers to the former things that Yahweh predicted. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and those predictions went out from my mouth]

Here, **my mouth** represents Yahweh’s act of speaking. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and I proclaimed them]

By **they came**, Yahweh means the events he had foretold actually happened. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [suddenly I did them and they came to pass]

4.note: The word translated as **Because** indicates that what follows is a reason for what comes after it. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what comes after it. Alternate translation: [The reason for this is that I knew]

The word **you** is singular here, even though Yahweh is addressing the whole nation of Israel. If your language distinguishes singular and plural forms of “you,” use whichever form is natural for addressing a group as a single person.

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people’s neck were **a sinew of iron**, that is, something that cannot be bent. He means that the people stubbornly refuse to obey him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and your neck is stiff and unbendable]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people’s forehead were **bronze**, that is, hard and unyielding. He means that the people stubbornly refuse to change. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and your forehead is hard and unyielding]

5.note: The word translated as **so** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [Therefore I declared]

Yahweh is using the word translated as **lest** to introduce an outcome that he does not want to happen. Because of this, he announced these things in advance so that this outcome would not happen. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that avoiding this outcome is the purpose of his announcing things in advance. Alternate translation: [so that you could not say]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [that your own idol did them]
The pronoun **them** refers to the things that Yahweh had predicted and then brought about. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [My idol did these things]

6.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb translated as **will you not declare** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to draw a contrast between what he has done for the Israelites, as he describes in verses 4–6, and what the Israelites should do in response. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [and for your part, will you not declare?]

Yahweh is using the question form to urge the people to acknowledge and declare what he has done. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [and for your part, you ought to declare1]

The words “you” and “your” and the implied “you” in the imperative **regard** are singular in verses 4–6 because Yahweh is addressing the Israelites as if they were an individual, their ancestor Jacob (verse 1). However, the word **you** is plural here because Yahweh is addressing the Israelites as a group, expecting each one of them to **declare** or testify that he has said in advance what would happen. So use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is using the adjective **new** as a noun to mean a certain kind of thing. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the new things]

Yahweh is using the adjective **hidden** as a noun to mean a certain kind of thing. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [and the hidden things]

7.note: Yahweh is using the word translated as **lest** to introduce an outcome that he does not want to happen. Because of this, he reveals these things only now so that this outcome would not happen. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that avoiding this outcome is the purpose. Alternate translation: [so that you could not say]

The expression **are created** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Now I am creating them]

The pronoun **they** refers to the new and hidden things that Yahweh has just mentioned. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Now these new and hidden things are created]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [that you already knew about this]

8.note: The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [since]

Isaiah is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [for I knew that you would surely betray me]

Yahweh is using **from the womb** as a common expression of the culture to mean “from the time you were born.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from the time you were born]

The expression **was called** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and from the womb, I called you “rebelling one”]

9.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what comes after it. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what comes after it. Alternate translation: [Because of]

Here, **my name** represents Yahweh’s reputation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [For the sake of my reputation]

Yahweh is using **lengthen my nose** as a common expression of the culture to mean “be patient” or “hold back my anger.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will hold back my anger]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **praise**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and for the sake of being praised]

Here, the words **so as not to cut you off** mark the purpose for which Yahweh restrains his anger against the people. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [to restrain myself from cutting you off]

10.note: Here Yahweh is speaking to the people of how he has tested and purified them as if he had **refined you, but not with silver**, the way a metalworker refines precious metal. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I have refined you, but not as one refines silver]

Some ancient manuscripts read “I have chosen you.” The ULT follows that reading. Other ancient manuscripts read “I have tested you.” If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.

Here Yahweh is speaking of the people’s time of suffering as if it were a **furnace of affliction** in which metal is refined. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in the midst of great suffering]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **affliction**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in the furnace where you were afflicted]

11.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what comes after it. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what comes after it. Alternate translation: [I will do this for my sake, for my sake]

Yahweh is repeating the phrase **For my sake** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [Surely for my sake]

Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that he will not allow his name to be dishonored. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [I will not allow my name to be profaned!]

The expression **be profaned** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [how should anyone profane my name]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **glory**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And I will not let another receive the honor that belongs to me]

12.note: The command **Listen** is singular here because Yahweh is addressing the nation of Israel as a single individual, calling it **Jacob**. If your language distinguishes singular and plural forms, use whichever is natural for addressing a whole people as one.

This is an imperative, but it communicates a polite request rather than a command. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please listen to me]

The expression **my called one** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and Israel, whom I have called]

Yahweh is using **I am he** as a common expression of the culture to mean that he alone is the one true and eternal God. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I alone am the eternal God]

Yahweh is referring to the whole of time by naming two extremes, **the first** and **the last**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [I existed before all things and will exist after all things]

13.note: Here, **my hand** represents Yahweh’s power. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my power founded the earth]

Here, **my right hand** represents Yahweh’s power. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and my power spread out the heavens]
The pronoun **them** refers to the earth and the heavens. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [I am calling to the earth and the heavens; they stand together]

Yahweh is speaking of **the earth** and **the heavens** as if they were living things that could **stand together** in his presence, ready to obey him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they rise up at once]

14.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that none of the idols predicted these things. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [None of them declared these things!]

The commands **Gather** and **hear** are plural, as the phrase **all of you** shows, because Yahweh is addressing a group of people. If your language distinguishes singular and plural command forms, use plural forms here.
The pronoun **them** refers to the idols and false gods of the nations. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Who among the idols declared these]

The pronoun **him** refers to the man whom Yahweh has chosen to act against Babylon. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh loves the man he has chosen; he will do his desire]

The implication is that Yahweh will accomplish his purpose against Babylon through this chosen man. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [through this man, Yahweh will accomplish his desire against Babylon]

Here, **his arm** represents the power that he will use against the Chaldeans. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and his strength against the Chaldeans]

15.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **I** repeatedly, even though the verb translated as **I have spoken** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize in the strongest way that it was he himself who did these things. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [I myself, Yahweh, am the one who has spoken]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the man’s undertaking as if it were a **way** or road along which he travels. He means that the man will succeed in what he sets out to do. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and he will succeed in what he does]

16.note: The commands **Draw near** and **hear** are plural, because Yahweh is addressing the whole group of people. If your language distinguishes singular and plural command forms, use plural forms here. Alternate translation: [All of you should draw near to me and hear this]

16.q: שָׁ֣ם אָ֑נִי וְ⁠עַתָּ֗ה אֲדֹנָ֧⁠י יְהוִ֛ה שְׁלָחַ֖⁠נִי
16.note: This is the end of what Yahweh said, beginning in verse 1 of this chapter; the words that follow are spoken by his servant. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could mark where Yahweh’s direct quotation ends and the new speaker begins.

17.note: The phrase **Thus says Yahweh** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language.

Yahweh is using this possessive form to mean that he is the one who redeems the people of Israel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh, the one who redeems you]

Yahweh is not using this possessive form **your God** to indicate that the people of Israel possess or control him. Rather, Yahweh is using these words to indicate that he is the God whom the people of Israel worship. Alternate translation: [am Yahweh, the God whom you worship]

The implication is that Yahweh teaches the people what will be for their own good. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the one teaching you what will benefit you]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the right way to live as if it were a **way** or road along which he leads the people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the one guiding you in how you should live]

18.note: Yahweh is making a conditional statement that sounds hypothetical, but he knows that the condition is not true. He is stating it as a condition to show that the peace and prosperity he goes on to describe also did not come about. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that the speaker believes is not true. Alternate translation: [You did not attend to my commandments, but if you had]

Yahweh is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of longing and grief. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [How I wish you had attended to my commandments]

The word **you** is singular here, even though Yahweh is addressing the whole nation of Israel. If your language distinguishes singular and plural forms of “you,” use whichever form is natural for addressing a group as a single person.

The point of this comparison is that just as **a river** flows continually and abundantly, so **your peace** would have been constant and plentiful. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Then your peace would have been continuous and abundant]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **peace**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [your peaceful life]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and your righteousness would have been like the waves of the sea]

The point of this comparison is that just as **the waves of the sea** keep coming without ceasing, so **your righteousness** would have continued without stopping. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and your righteousness, like waves of the sea that never stop coming]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and your right actions]

19.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the sand** is too plentiful to count, so **your seed** would have been very numerous. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [And your seed would have been as numerous and uncountable as the sand]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the people’s descendants as if they were **seed** that a person plants. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your offspring]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and the offspring of your womb would have been like its grains]

The point of this comparison is that just as **its grains** are too many to count, so **the offspring of your womb** would have been very numerous. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and the offspring of your womb would have been as numerous as its grains]
Yahweh is using this possessive form to mean the children who would come from your own body. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the children born to you]

The expression **been cut off** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I would not have cut him off]

The pronoun **He** refers to the people’s descendants, spoken of together as a single group. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Your offspring would not have been cut off]

The expression **been destroyed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and I would not have destroyed his name]

Yahweh is using **from to my face** as a common expression of the culture to mean “from my presence.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from my presence]

20.note: The commands **Go out** and **flee** are plural, because Yahweh is addressing all the people of Israel. If your language distinguishes singular and plural command forms, use plural forms here.

Here, **the Chaldeans** represents the land that the Chaldeans rule. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from the land of the Chaldeans]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **singing**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [With a song] or [By singing a song]

Yahweh is using **to the end of the earth** as a common expression of the culture to mean “to the most distant places in the world.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to the most distant places in the world]
The word **say** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly.

21.q: וְ⁠לֹ֣א צָמְא֗וּ בָּ⁠חֳרָבוֹת֙ הֽוֹלִיכָ֔⁠ם מַ֥יִם מִ⁠צּ֖וּר הִזִּ֣יל לָ֑⁠מוֹ וַ⁠יִּ֨בְקַע־צ֔וּר וַ⁠יָּזֻ֖בוּ מָֽיִם
21.note: Some interpreters believe that the quotation at the end of verse 20 continues through to the end of this verse. You may want to follow the major translation in your area.

If this is not the Judean exiles describing how Yahweh cared for them during their return from Babylon, then it is Isaiah reminding them how Yahweh cared for the Israelites when he brought them from Egypt to Canaan. The implication is that Yahweh will care for the Judeans in the same way. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And you will not thirst, just as your ancestors did not when Yahweh led them in desolations]
The pronoun **they** refers to the people of Israel, whom Yahweh redeemed. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The people of Israel did not thirst]

22.note: The phrase **says Yahweh** identifies Yahweh as the speaker of this direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating the speaker of a quotation in your language.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **peace**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Nothing is peaceful]

Yahweh is using the adjective **wicked** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [for those who are wicked]
